newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH PX50 CLOSES LOWER BUT IPB PULLS BACK.
newsitem.headline: CZECH PX50 CLOSES LOWER BUT IPB PULLS BACK.

text.p: Czech shares continued to slide on Thursday in a session dominated by rumours and a strong official denial of heavy 1996 losses at one of the country's biggest banks, IPB a.s.
IPB is due to release audited 1996 results in the next few days and rumours swept the share and bond markets that the bank would post large losses.

At one point IPB had fallen 25 crowns, 7.6 percent, on the bourse to 305 but after a high ranking IPB spokesman told Reuters that the rumours were "nonsense" it recovered, to close down just one crown at 329.

"In the morning there was genuine panic as there were several people selling at very low prices in the bond and the share. Then this story came out and said it was a bunch of nonsense," said John Vax, director of capital markets at ING Barings.
Vax added that most traders would probably wait for the actual results before making further buy or sell decisions.
Overall, the PX50 index lost 6.2 points, 1.12 percent, to 547.2 dragged down by losses to most major issues
